researcher_notes: Shell/BPL had planned a standalone LNG regas terminal at Clifton Pier (active in 2020-2021, EIA released June 2021). The plan went quiet after Sept 2021 and by mid-2024 was effectively shelved: in June 2024 the government/minister announced LNG would instead supply a new 177MW combined-cycle plant at Blue Hills, with NO mention of the Clifton Pier LNG terminal (Nassau Guardian, 11 Jun 2024, verified 2024+Clifton Pier). 2024 = the documented pivot/shelving inflection. CAVEAT: the 'shelved' label is inferred from the mid-2024 pivot (the source does not use the word 'shelved'), and the project was subsequently REVIVED in a modified FOCOL-Shell JV form in March 2025 (dredging began 2025). An alternative reading dates the shelving to 2021 (project went silent), but no source ties a year to an explicit 'shelved/suspended' event; 2024 is the best-verifiable milestone. Single independent source -> tier low.

AES's Ocean Express/Ocean Cay LNG import project (Bimini) was proposed early 2000s, EIA approved Oct 2003, final approval expected 2008 but never granted amid citizen/environmental opposition. It was effectively abandoned when, in August 2009, AES announced it would lease/sell the terminal site to a Bahamian-incorporated company after failing to obtain a government decision; the terminal was never built. 2009 is the clearest DATED end-of-project marker (per WikiLeaks cables it was 'eventually scrapped'; AES nominally retained a re-lease option, so 2009 is a de-facto abandonment, not a formal termination announcement). CAVEAT: the detailed project retellings (offshore-technology / hydrocarbons-technology / oilandgasadvancement) share one underlying text = a single source; only the oilandgasadvancement host verified (the other two return HTTP 403). No genuinely independent second source found tying a specific year to the cancellation -> tier low, independent false.

No retirement year exists to find: the Puerto Brisa (Terminal Brisa, La Guajira/Dibulla) LNG import & regasification terminal was NEVER BUILT and never operated. It is a still-live PLANNED project (developer Energy Developments LLC with TransEnergy LNG; land lease signed 2021; Kogas-Tech engineering) that as of Nov 2024 was being described in the future tense ('construirán'/'they will build' - Forbes Colombia, verified 2024+Puerto Brisa). The GEM record's status 'retired' with substatus 'planned' is contradictory and appears to be a data anomaly: a project that never entered operation cannot have a retirement/decommission year. UNRESOLVED per brief guidance (never operated -> no defensible retirement year). Recommend flagging the retired+planned combination to the user for correction (likely should be proposed/planned, not retired). NOTE: distinct from the Puerto Brisa COAL terminal (built 2014, coal ops suspended 2017).

No defensible proposal year found. Dunkerque LNG has expressed a broad, undated FUTURE ambition to develop 'new molecules' business lines (CO2, hydrogen, ammonia imports/exports) leveraging its cold-management infrastructure - stated e.g. by its commercial director in April 2023 ('Nous devons developper... le role de Dunkerque LNG dans l'ecosysteme des nouvelles molecules (CO2, hydrogene, ammoniac...)', newsletterdunkerquelng.com/actu/415). But this is an aspirational strategy mention, not a distinct dated PROPOSAL/announcement of an ammonia import terminal. No press release, regulator filing, or FEED/open-season specifically announcing an ammonia import terminal at Dunkerque with an identifiable year could be verified; GEM's own record leaves the proposal year blank. Concrete Dunkerque decarbonisation projects that DID advance are CO2 (Air Liquide 'D'Artagnan'/CO2 export, 2024), not ammonia. Earliest defensible ammonia mention is 2022-2023 but too vague to tie to a proposal milestone. UNRESOLVED (ammonia is also out of GEM update scope per brief).

No construction-start year exists to find. 'Expansion 2' is the +2 mtpa (~+2.0 bcm/y) capacity increase from Elengy/Fosmax's 'Open Season Fos Cavaou 2021' (launched March 2021), offered for delivery 'from April 2030 until 2045 or beyond'. It is a capacity/regulatory-debottlenecking expansion planned to be developed 'as of 2030', with NO reported FID and NO physical groundbreaking/site works; Elengy's 2021-2024 activity was capacity auctions/subscriptions, not construction. (Expansion 1, the +to-10-mtpa debottlenecking, went operating in 2023.) GEM's own timeline leaves Expansion 2's construction year blank while carrying status 'construction'. Because no site works have been publicly reported and no source dates a construction start, there is no verifiable construction-start year. UNRESOLVED. Proposal year, if wanted, would be 2021 (open season launch), but the requested milestone here is construction-start.

FSRU idled in 2019: the Gazprom Kaliningrad FSRU Marshal Vasilevskiy was installed at the offshore terminal Jan 2019 but received NO regas deliveries after arriving laden; it was promptly offered on the spot market as an LNG carrier (March-July 2019) and chartered to OMV as floating storage off Rotterdam (Aug-Nov 2019). It essentially never operated as an FSRU at station and was redeployed as a conventional carrier from 2019. Argus ('Kaliningrad FSRU set to return to Russian exclave', verified 2019+Marshal Vasilevskiy) and LNG Industry (29 Aug 2019 'Russia leases FSRU to OMV', verified 2019+Marshal Vasilevskiy) independently document the 2019 idling/redeployment. Later: brief return to Kaliningrad early 2022, largely idle since with only occasional cargoes; still not steadily used as an FSRU as of 2025 - but the FIRST idling milestone is 2019. Russian-language search corroborated the same narrative; English sources used as they contain the year+token cleanly.

New Fortress Energy's Sri Lanka LNG package (signed Sept 2021: 40% of the Yugadanavi/Kerawalapitiya plant + an unsolicited offshore Colombo LNG receiving/storage/regas terminal + pipeline/floating storage) collapsed in 2022. The Morning (Colombo) reported on 29 Nov 2022 that 'New Fortress Energy [is] pulling out of Yugadanavi', withdrawing from the whole agreement incl. the LNG import terminal and floating storage complex - the clearest DATED cancellation/withdrawal event for the NFE-specific project. The government subsequently (Aug 2023) moved to let a different developer (Petronet LNG) take the terminal, confirming the death, but that later narrative is mostly documented via GEM (not citable) and via EconomyNext (bot-blocked 403 - couldn't verify). CITATION NOTE: The Morning's original URL is now dead (404); cited via its live Wayback snapshot (ts 1669755889 = 29 Nov 2022), which passes the verifier for 2022 + Yugadanavi + 'pulling out' + New Fortress. Single contemporaneous primary-press source directly on the milestone -> tier medium. NB distinct from the older 'Kerewalapitiya LNG Terminal' (Petronet/Engro) GEM record.
